source_text: Retractans igitur in primo opere meo sententiam eius, qua dixerat: Nam sicut peccatum, sive hinc, sive inde trahatur a parvulis, opus est diaboli; sic homo, sive hinc, sive inde nascatur, opus est Dei [n23] ; ita autem a me nunc hic refertur, sicut in meo opere continetur, unde maximam partem fuerat iste furatus.
pass_a_gloss: Reviewing therefore in my first work his sentence by which he had said: For just as sin, whether it is drawn from here or from there by little children, is a work of the devil; so a human being, whether he is born from here or from there, is a work of God; it is however now here reported by me just as it is contained in my work, from which this man had stolen a very great part.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: In my first work, then, I examined his statement: ‘For just as sin, whether infants derive it from this source or that, is the devil’s work, so a human being, whether born from this source or that, is God’s work’ (Augustine, Marriage and Desire 1.1). I quote it here as it stands in my own work, from which this man had stolen a very large portion.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
